name: parallax-scroll
props: The screen's content, under the header.
Fills the header area: a photo, a map, a gallery (wins over headerImage).
Shortcut for a full-bleed header photo.
Describes headerImage for screen readers (skipped when omitted).
Header height, including the part under the status bar.
How the header moves while scrolling up: 0 scrolls with the content, 1 stays pinned while the content slides over it.
iOS: pulling down stretches the header to fill the gap, anchored at the top. Turn off with a refreshControl.
Pinned to the bottom of the header (a title over the photo); lifts and fades as it scrolls away, over a bottom scrim.
Ready-made top bar (theme background, hairline, centred title) that fades in once the header has scrolled under it.
Your own bar instead: fills the bar area (topInset included) and fades in the same way. Decorative — buttons go in barLeft / barRight.
Buttons pinned to the bar, visible over the photo too: each child sits on a round theme-coloured bubble that melts into the bar. Pass an array for several.
Height of the bar row, below topInset.
Space above the bar for the status bar / notch — pass your safe-area top inset.
Style for the content under the header (padding, gap, background — theme background by default).
Style for the outer frame (size, margins, radius). Fills its parent by default.
JS handler called alongside the native parallax event. For UI-thread effects use useParallaxScroll().scroll instead of your own Animated.event.
Forwarded to the scroll view, so you can call scrollTo.
Everything else is passed to the scroll view (vertical only): refreshControl, onScrollEndDrag, nestedScrollEnabled…
How much slower than its frame the photo moves: 0 still, 1 fixed on screen, negative the other way.
Bottom gradient so white text reads on the photo.
Content over the photo, aligned to the bottom (a caption, a tag).
Describes the photo for screen readers.
Style for the frame / for the photo itself.
Offset relative to the scroll: positive lags behind the content, negative leads it.
What drifts, and its style (the transform is taken by the parallax).
The live scroll offset (native-driver friendly), viewport size and content size for your own effects; null outside a ParallaxScrollView.
